subsection: S13.1 Background. The full benchmark was carried out on a single laptop, an NVIDIA RTX 4060 Laptop GPU (8 GB, CUDA). To check that the reported scores are hardware-invariant, one identical configuration - the full DALS optimizer on CIFAR-100 - was also run on a second laptop that differs only in its GPU. As Table S13.1 shows, both are Ada Lovelace consumer laptop GPUs with 8 GB of GDDR6 VRAM, a 128-bit memory bus, and 256 GB/s of memory bandwidth; the only material difference is the CUDA-core count (3072 vs. 4608). These specifications are documented in References [1-5]. This section concerns the reported score (accuracy) only; runtime is not the object of comparison, and the anchor below is the only experiment in this study executed on two GPUs.

S13.2 Repeated-anchor calibration. To measure the device effect directly on the reported metric, we trained one identical configuration - the full DALS optimizer on CIFAR-100 (ConvNet, five seeds) - once on each GPU. As Table S13.2 shows, the two means agree to within one point: 53.04 (RTX 4070) and 53.99 (RTX 4060), a difference of about 0.95 points, i.e. 0.99 when both are read at the reported precision. The two devices are therefore calibrated against each other on a task drawn from the paper's own benchmark. Since the tasks' memory demand is well within the 8 GB shared by both GPUs (Section S7), both configurations are more than sufficient for these experiments, and - as the anchor shows - they produce highly similar scores.
